obligations.note: The new branch in rbac.is_allowed grants any 'report:<X>' action to every role holding <X>, e.g. ('treasury_manager','report:release_payment') and ('auditor','report:export_ledger'). These actions are not in ACTIONS or the approved access policy, so they are allowed without being decided explicitly or approved, which breaks default-deny. The exhaustive ACC-1 control test only probes declared actions and the literal 'unlisted_action', so its pass does not cover these names.

Auditor grants are unchanged and none is state-changing, so the alias only maps to auditor read grants. The registered exhaustive control test_auditor_is_read_only passed in the CI run on head 82712f6.

it_admin holds no approve_payment or release_payment grant, so 'report:approve_payment' and 'report:release_payment' are still denied to it. The exhaustive control test_it_admin_cannot_approve_or_release passed on head.
Ticket CHG-24775 (standard) was approved by change manager erik.brandt on 2026-10-18T00:44Z, before the change opened. Its components [payments.access] cover the only touched file, rbac.py.
The code_review approval is from mara.costa, a payments change_approver and a different person from the author sofia.santos (p-ssantos).
Both approvals name head commit 82712f6, the only commit in the change.

records/ci/run.json shows a successful ci/run-tests.sh baseline-payments run on 82712f6: 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped, including the ACC-1, ACC-2 and SOD-1 control tests. I could not rerun locally because pytest is not installed.
rbac.py (payments.access) is security_sensitive. A security_review approval from kofi.mensah, a security_reviewer, names head 82712f6.

No exception in the register covers ACC-1 or payments.access, so none excuses the ACC-1 deviation. The register entries that exist are for other obligations and components, or are expired or withdrawn.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers rbac.py, so this change does not lapse any recorded evidence.

summary: The process records are in order: the ticket is approved and covers the right component, there are independent code and security reviews on the head commit, and the head-commit CI run is green. But the change adds a 'report:' prefix alias in rbac.is_allowed that grants undeclared, unapproved actions to every role holding the underlying action. That violates ACC-1's requirement that every role and action pair be decided explicitly and that anything not granted be denied. The exhaustive ACC-1 control misses this because it never probes 'report:' names. No exception covers the deviation, so the change is rejected.
